title: fix(plugin-approvals): the delegation form's Delegator picker offers only the signed-in user
body:
Fixes #24764

Clause-②: no

## What changed

`sys_approval_delegation.delegator_id` now declares a picker filter:

```ts
lookupFilters: [{ field: 'id', operator: 'eq', value: '{current_user_id}' }],
```

The delegation write guard (`bindDelegationWriteGuard` in `packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/lifecycle-hooks.ts`) accepts one delegator on a non-system write: the acting user. Its docstring records the decision: "a delegation names its own author as delegator; acting for someone else is done through the approval-level override". The field was a free `sys_user` lookup, so Approvals → Delegations → New offered every user, and the server refused all but one of them with 403. The picker now offers the signed-in user and nobody else.

- **Landing.** `packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/sys-approval-delegation.object.ts`, where the card expected it.
- **Unchanged.** The guard: no refusal is widened and there is no admin exemption. The field stays `required`. What a write may store does not change, because nothing on the write path reads `lookupFilters`.
- **Not touched.** No spec edit, no objectui edit, no consumer-side mapping. `approval-service.ts` is not touched.

## Why this vocabulary (measured)

- `lookupFilters` is the spec's structured picker filter (`packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts`). In the pinned console (objectui `12dc7b47c3`, `.objectui-sha`), `LookupField` lowers each entry through `lookupFiltersToRecord` (`eq` becomes `{ id: value }`). It sends the result as the `$filter` of its candidate query, and the popover, the record-picker dialog, the people picker and the recents rail all use that query.
- The engine resolves `{current_user_id}` in a read's `where` against the caller (`ObjectQL.resolveWhereTokens`, the one gate every server read passes). `@objectstack/lint`'s filter-token rule already covers `lookupFilters` (`validate-filter-tokens.test.ts`).
- M4 (order on insert) measured: `applyFieldDefaults` runs, then the `beforeInsert` hooks (where the guard stamps an omitted delegator), then record validation (`required`). Nothing here needed `required` changed.

## Route not taken: a `current_user` default (raised as a decision in the report)

Option (ii) from the dispatch, `defaultValue: 'current_user'`, is honoured by the pinned console: create forms seed the acting user on a `sys_user` lookup (`plugin-form/src/schemaDefaults.ts`). It would open the form on the one value the guard accepts. I measured it on the real engine at this branch, as an insert that omits `delegator_id`. It changes exactly one cell of the write accept set:

| caller | base | with the default |
|---|---|---|
| member `u_admin` | stored `u_admin` (the guard stamps it) | stored `u_admin` |
| anonymous, non-system | refused, `FORBIDDEN` 403 | refused, `FORBIDDEN` 403 |
| system, no user id | refused, `VALIDATION_FAILED` (`required`) | refused, `VALIDATION_FAILED` |
| system, user id `u_svc` | refused, `VALIDATION_FAILED` (`required`) | **stored `u_svc`** |

No HTTP door produces a system context, and no code in this repo writes delegation rows. Even so, it is an accept-set change, and the claim's `Clause-②: no` does not cover one. The picker filter alone makes the form offer only what the guard accepts, so this PR does not add the default and leaves it for a decision. The first commit on this branch carried the default, and the second removed it after the measurement. The net diff has no default.

## Tests

New file: `packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/sys-approval-delegation-delegator-picker.test.ts`. It runs a real `ObjectQL` over `SqlDriver` (better-sqlite3, in-memory, real DDL) with the guard bound, and asserts:

1. the declaration, read off the object and off the registered body;
2. the picker's candidate query returns the caller and nobody else, for each of three callers (the declared filter, lowered the way the console lowers it);
3. the guard accepts every candidate the picker offers;
4. the guard is not widened: a create naming another user is refused with `FORBIDDEN` / 403, and so is an update relabelling the delegator, and nothing is stored;
5. `required` stays.

Ablations, each through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`: the anchor hit once, the blob changed on disk, the test ran, and the file was restored to the HEAD blob with `git diff HEAD` empty. The test imports the object and the guard from `src/` by relative path, so no `dist/` is involved.

- **A1, drop the filter.** 6 failed, 3 passed. The picker offers `[u_admin, u_priya, u_tomas]` instead of `[caller]`, both declaration pins fail (`expected undefined to deeply equal`), and the guard refuses an offered candidate.
- **A2, put a foreign delegator back into the guard** (`if (false && has && supplied !== userId) deny();`). 2 failed, 7 passed: both refusal pins, with "promise resolved instead of rejecting".
- **A3, `required: false` on the delegator.** 2 failed, 7 passed: the declaration pin, and "`required` stays" (the promise resolved instead of rejecting).

### Readings at head `529f78b82` (after the last commit; `main` merged in at `307ce4c4b`)

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-approvals exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2`: 87 files, 1156 tests passed, exit 0.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-approvals typecheck`: exit 0. `check:test-typecheck: OK`, and the debt ledger is unchanged (8 files, 324 errors, 27 signatures).
- Local gate subset: the 68 commands `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derives for this diff all exit 0, and `--ran` reconciles 68 derived, 68 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED. The same 68-command list derives at `origin/main` `c3a8e07b6` with these three files applied.
- Repo-wide runs (`pnpm lint`, `test:repo` and the full farm) are left to this PR's CI.

## Out of scope (the seat files these)

- **The console says nothing when the 403 comes back** (objectui's half of the card). At the pin, `ModalForm`'s submit `catch` hands the error to `schema.onError` and rethrows. It shows no toast and no field error of its own, so the dialog just stays open. objectui#13161 does not cover it: that card is about the action-param dialog, which closes on a server error and shows a toast.

## Acceptance notes

- The edit form's Delegator picker narrows to the acting user too. That matches the guard on update, which refuses a delegator other than the caller.
- `lookupFilters` is presentation only. The guard remains the enforcement, and this PR claims nothing beyond the picker.
